# Model completeness

<!-- Generated by scripts/completeness/report.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Whether the model of each CCNL is complete, so that only the comparison
with real payslips is left. A CCNL is complete when its census lists its
requirements and nothing the model owes it is open: no open requirement,
no weak payable rule (`assumed` or `missing`) it reads, no open limitation
with a monetary impact, none whose fact has no input (`outside_input`),
and no capability left to the caller, partial or not computed.
Completeness is not readiness and not external validation: readiness is
shown for reference only, and
[the validation matrix](validation-matrix.md) tracks the comparisons.
`scripts/completeness/report.py --strict` fails while any CCNL is
incomplete.

**Complete: 0/132 CCNLs.** Bundle: 268 weak rules, 556 open limitations (556 with a monetary impact).

## Declared window

Every CCNL is assessed from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31, the supported tax years. Pay tables that start after the first day or end before the last are a gap of the CCNL. The history the engine reads from before the window (the INPS sickness base of the month before, the progressive amounts of the year) comes from the opening state and the prior-year facts of the request, not from the bundle.

Future data, registered apart from the gaps: a contract whose validity ends inside the window keeps its last tables until the renewal (column *Renewal due*), and these resources carry the values of the year before because their sources are not published yet (their weak rules and the engine limitations `provisional_inps_ruleset`, `provisional_ruleset` are not counted as gaps):

- `contribution/2027/agricoltura.json`
- `contribution/2027/artigianato.json`
- `contribution/2027/credito.json`
- `contribution/2027/edilizia.json`
